title: Ang 1094–1102: Maru Var M5
hookLine: Guru Arjan's ballad with short couplets
tomorrow: why would a book of peace praise a warrior?

cards: The morning of the class talk, Simran was already at the door, backpack on, slides on her phone, stomach in knots.

Bebe Jaswant came out of the kitchen with flour still on her hands, took Simran's hand anyway, and whispered something in Punjabi. Then she let go and went back to her rotis like nothing had happened.
Simran had heard her say the same line before exams, and before Jas's wedding. She never explained it. It turns out the line lives on today's pages, in Guru Arjan's Maru ballad.

teach.b: From ang 1094 comes Maru Var by Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru. Like other vars, it climbs in pauris, stanzas like steps.

But its saloks carry a heading of their own, dakhne: short couplets in a regional Punjabi speech, compact enough to carry around in your pocket. That's what Bebe does. One of them, on ang 1096, is her line.

teach.h: WHEN YOU ARE ON MY SIDE.
teach.b: In paraphrase: when You are on my side, what is there to worry about? Notice what it doesn't say.

It doesn't promise the talk will go well, or the exam, or the wedding. It doesn't say God is on my side against anyone. It turns the question around: not, will this go right? but, who am I standing with?
When the answer is the One, the worry loses its grip, even if the outcome is still unknown. That's why it fits a door, a waiting room, a morning with knots in your stomach. It's short on purpose.
A ballad about heroes, and its hero's whole armor is one couplet: You are on my side. Bebe never explained it because she didn't need to. She just put it in Simran's hand with the flour.

how: Guru Arjan's Maru Var is sung in kirtan pauri by pauri with its dakhne; some Sikhs keep a line like 'jaa tooN meraa val hai' close and repeat it before a hard day.

s: the line promises that whatever you're facing will turn out well
it asks who you stand with, not whether things go right.
Guru Arjan's Maru Var has saloks headed dakhne, short couplets
compact enough to carry, the way Bebe does.
'on my side' means God takes my side against other people
the couplet is about company in a hard moment, not winning against anyone.

games.q: your friend is about to sit an exam she's dreading and asks if Bebe's line means she'll pass. what does the couplet actually offer?
o: company: whatever the result, she isn't facing it alone.
a guarantee: say it with faith and the grade comes out fine.
nothing, unless she's already ready for the exam.
games.why: 'when You are on my side, what is there to worry about' turns the question from the outcome to the company.

practice: Bring to mind one hard thing coming up this week. Then, under your breath, say the name of someone who's on your side, or if you pray, a short line you trust. Let the hard thing stay where it is, and rest in the company instead.
